newsitem.title: GERMANY: Soybeans lead steady Oct/Dec EU oilseeds crush.
newsitem.headline: Soybeans lead steady Oct/Dec EU oilseeds crush.

text.p: Oilseeds processing in the European Union in fourth quarter 1996 was broadly unchanged from a year earlier as higher soybean and sunseed crushings offset a lower rapeseed figure, Oil World newsletter said.
The independent publication put the Oct/Dec soybean crush at 4.02 million tonnes (3.75 million a year earlier), sunseed at 1.73 million (1.48) and rapeseed at 1.60 million (2.09).
Higher soybean crushings were reported in Germany, France, Belgium and Britain.
Sunseed crushings, mostly of imported eastern European seed, were up in Spain, France, Belgium, Germany and Holland.
Rapeseed crushings were down because of high prices, tight supply and unsatisfactory margins, Oil World said.
The EU probably also exported more rapeseed to Poland than previously thought.

Poland, in recent years a net exporter, reportedly has been buying rapeseed from the EU (Germany, France, Britain, Denamrk), as well as from Hungary, the Ukraine and the Czech and Slovak republics -- turning into a net importer.
EU oil output in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the three seeds totalled 2.08 million tonnes (2.15 million in 95) while meal output was 5.04 million (5.01 million previously).
